import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# Filter out rows with missing values in relevant columns
df_filtered = df.dropna(subset=['AlterV10Lang', 'SexLang', 'AnzHunde'])

# Group by age group and owner gender, calculate mean number of dogs
grouped = df_filtered.groupby(['AlterV10Lang', 'SexLang'])['AnzHunde'].mean().reset_index()

# Pivot to get male and female as columns
pivot_df = grouped.pivot(index='AlterV10Lang', columns='SexLang', values='AnzHunde').reset_index()

# Order the age groups based on AlterV10Sort
# First, get the original dataframe's order
age_order = df.drop_duplicates('AlterV10Lang').sort_values('AlterV10Sort')['AlterV10Lang'].tolist()

# Plotting
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
sns.barplot(data=pivot_df.melt(id_vars='AlterV10Lang', value_vars=['männlich', 'weiblich'], 
                               var_name='Owner Gender', value_name='Avg Number of Dogs'),
            x='AlterV10Lang', y='Avg Number of Dogs', hue='Owner Gender', order=age_order)

plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.title('Average Number of Dogs per Owner by Age Group and Gender')
plt.xlabel('Owner Age Group')
plt.ylabel('Average Number of Dogs')
plt.legend(title='Owner Gender')
plt.tight_layout()

plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
